title: Casablanca Valley
description: Chile's cool coastal pioneer: crisp Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay cooled by the Pacific.
L: The Casablanca Valley lies between Santiago and the port of Valparaíso, about 30 km from the Pacific. It runs east to west, opening to the ocean, which lets cool sea air and fog flow in. It has about 6,000 hectares of vines, mostly on gentle slopes and valley floors.

The cold Humboldt Current runs north along Chile's coast, chilling the ocean. Each morning, fog and cool air move into Casablanca, burning off by midday. Summers are much cooler than in the Central Valley. Spring frost is a major risk; growers use wind machines and sprinklers. Water is scarce, as there's no big river.
The cold Humboldt Current and morning fog
Ocean air and fog cool the valley.

Before the late 1980s, Chile's vineyards were mostly in the warm Central Valley. In 1982, Pablo Morandé planted vines in Casablanca, then thought too cold. Its success with white wines opened the way for other cool coastal valleys, like San Antonio, Leyda and Limarí. Casablanca showed Chile could make cool-climate wine.
Casablanca was planted before the warm Central Valley.
Not true. It was planted from the 1980s, after the Central Valley.

Describe its Chardonnay and Pinot Noir

Sauvignon Blanc is Casablanca's leading grape, giving crisp wines with citrus, grapefruit, passion fruit, cut grass and a herbal, saline note. The cool climate keeps acidity high and green aromas fresh. It's often compared with New Zealand's style, though usually a little less pungent.

Chardonnay gives fresh, citrus and stone fruit wines, often with some oak and lees. Pinot Noir gives light, fresh reds with red cherry and strawberry. Syrah, from cooler sites, gives peppery wines. About three-quarters of Casablanca's vineyards are white, which is unusual in red-dominated Chile.
Match each grape to its Casablanca style.
Casablanca Sauvignon Blanc is often great value, with fresh, zesty fruit similar to New Zealand's.
Why do white grapes dominate Casablanca?

Reading Casablanca and eating with it

Labels show the grape and Valle de Casablanca, often with Costa, the coastal descriptor added in 2011. Casablanca is part of the larger Aconcagua region. Chile's 85% rules apply. Many large Chilean wineries have Casablanca vineyards for their whites.

Casablanca Sauvignon Blanc suits Chilean seafood: ceviche, machas, razor clams, congrio, conger eel, and goat's cheese and salads. Chardonnay suits crab, chicken and creamy fish; Pinot Noir suits salmon and duck. Serve whites at 7 to 10 degrees, Pinot at 14 to 15.
Which dish suits Casablanca Sauvignon Blanc?
Citrus and acidity match the lime-cured fish.
Valparaíso, near Casablanca, is famous for seafood, a natural pairing with the valley's crisp whites.
